newsitem.title: UK: JAL not planning ex-UK air cargo rate rise.
newsitem.headline: JAL not planning ex-UK air cargo rate rise.

text.p: Japan Airlines Co Ltd is not planning a spring increase in ex-UK air cargo rates, the airline's cargo sales manager, Tony Edwards told Reuters.
"We were looking at an April rise. But the outlook is unclear, with people neither optimistic nor pessimistic," he added.
"The continued strength of sterling is a worry. Additionally, a two percent increase in the Japanese consumption tax to five percent on April 1 is likely to hit imports," he said.
"It is a question of wait and see. If business is booming, we will put up rates later in the year," Edwards added.
He said that the six pence a kg fuel surcharge for ex-UK air cargo applied since late 1996 by JAL and other airlines, will remain in place for the time being.

On Tuesday British Airways World Cargo announced range of ex-UK air cargo rate rises from March 17, including a seven percent increase for cargo to Japan. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom - Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +5017
